chapter: Wax Records, Broadway shows and Eddie Condon
title: Touring with Eddie Condon and Cliff Jackson
summary: Hall tells of the eighteen-day tour with Condon, Lee Wiley and others after playing Condon's club.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: To prove it, so when they did deliver it they left them out on the sidewalk. So, and meanwhile, I was working with Eddie Condon, traveling on the road with him.
When did that start?
In '46, and --
Oh, so this was before you really went into the band, the shows?
Yeah.
It was in---
Yeah, it was inbetween this, when I was at Philadelphia with Eddie Davis at the Watts.
Oh, at the Watts Club.
I left there and went --
Oh, with Eddie Condon?
With Eddie Condon and toured with Cliff Jackson, one of the most wonderful tours I ever had. What was the name of the singer?
(Inaudible). Lee Wiley?
(Inaudible) and her husband,
now I can get the names, - Jess Stacey (phonetic), Ernie Cacerfas, Bobby Hackett, Joe Thomas.
Where did you tour? All over the country?
Well, no, we did 18 cities, we did 14 cities something like that in 18 days. Here to Cleveland, St. Louis, Buffalo to Canada, you know.
How did you happen to get hooked up with them?
Well, I had been working with Eddie down in the Village. When I was substituting for Sid Weiss or Jack either Lesberg or somebody.
When did that start, a little earlier in the forties?
In '46 when they --
Opened his club? So, you've been with all kinds of, you know, styles in the music.
Without being egotistical, I can say I have covered the field.
